question: A utility manages 14 separate sewer basins with one renewal budget. Which input set gives the most defensible order for scheduling basin rehabilitation?
correctAnswer: Basin rankings built from flow records, condition grades and failure consequence ratings
explanation: At system scale, limited renewal funds go furthest when basins are ranked by measured risk. Construction order, seniority and one month of requests do not show likelihood or consequence of failure.
options: Basin rankings built from flow records, condition grades and failure consequence ratings
The calendar order in which each basin was originally constructed and commissioned for service
Recommendations from the crew members who have worked in the system for the longest time
The number of service requests received from each basin during the past month alone
optionA: Basin rankings built from flow records, condition grades and failure consequence ratings
optionB: The calendar order in which each basin was originally constructed and commissioned for service
optionC: Recommendations from the crew members who have worked in the system for the longest time
optionD: The number of service requests received from each basin during the past month alone
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Which set of elements belongs together in a CMOM program for a large collection system?
correctAnswer: Capacity assurance, management structure, operations and overflow response planning
explanation: CMOM combines capacity assurance, management, operations and maintenance, and overflow response into one managed program. Purchasing and administrative items support the utility but are not CMOM program elements.
options: Capacity assurance, management structure, operations and overflow response planning
Capacity assurance, vehicle purchasing, office layout and staff social event planning
Management structure, uniform supply, fuel contracts and seasonal decoration schedules
Overflow response planning, radio procurement, parking permits and holiday rosters only
optionA: Capacity assurance, management structure, operations and overflow response planning
optionB: Capacity assurance, vehicle purchasing, office layout and staff social event planning
optionC: Management structure, uniform supply, fuel contracts and seasonal decoration schedules
optionD: Overflow response planning, radio procurement, parking permits and holiday rosters only
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: A basin study splits a large sewershed into smaller sub-basins before flow monitoring begins. What does that split allow the program to do?
correctAnswer: Compare I&I contributions area by area so removal work targets the worst sources first
explanation: Monitoring at sub-basin outlets lets the program compare I&I rates between areas and rank removal work. The split does not equalize rates, remove the need for rain data, or replace source investigation.
options: Compare I&I contributions area by area so removal work targets the worst sources first
Guarantee that every sub-basin will show exactly the same I&I rate during the study period
Eliminate the need to measure rainfall anywhere inside the study area during storms
Replace all later smoke testing and manhole inspection work planned for the basin
optionA: Compare I&I contributions area by area so removal work targets the worst sources first
optionB: Guarantee that every sub-basin will show exactly the same I&I rate during the study period
optionC: Eliminate the need to measure rainfall anywhere inside the study area during storms
optionD: Replace all later smoke testing and manhole inspection work planned for the basin
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: In an RDII analysis, the R value assigned to a sub-basin describes which relationship?
correctAnswer: The share of rainfall volume over the area that enters the sanitary sewer as RDII
explanation: The R value is the fraction of rainfall volume over the contributing area that appears in the sewer as rainfall derived inflow and infiltration. It is a volume relationship, not a size, budget or dry weather ratio.
options: The share of rainfall volume over the area that enters the sanitary sewer as RDII
The ratio of the sewer diameter to the depth of the deepest manhole in the sub-basin
The share of the annual maintenance budget that the sub-basin consumed last year
The ratio of night flow to average day flow measured during dry weather periods
optionA: The share of rainfall volume over the area that enters the sanitary sewer as RDII
optionB: The ratio of the sewer diameter to the depth of the deepest manhole in the sub-basin
optionC: The share of the annual maintenance budget that the sub-basin consumed last year
optionD: The ratio of night flow to average day flow measured during dry weather periods
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria

question: A Class 3 operator reviews overnight run data from 22 lift stations each morning. Which stations should receive the first field visit?
correctAnswer: Stations showing abnormal run times, repeated starts or high level alarms overnight
explanation: Abnormal run times, frequent starts and high level alarms signal developing failures that can become overflows. Distance, recent cleaning and pump age alone do not indicate overnight problems.
options: Stations showing abnormal run times, repeated starts or high level alarms overnight
Stations located closest to the works yard, visited in the order they appear on the map
Stations that received a full cleaning during the previous month, checked once again
Stations with the newest pumps, because new equipment needs the closest watching
optionA: Stations showing abnormal run times, repeated starts or high level alarms overnight
optionB: Stations located closest to the works yard, visited in the order they appear on the map
optionC: Stations that received a full cleaning during the previous month, checked once again
optionD: Stations with the newest pumps, because new equipment needs the closest watching

question: Which records form the core operating history for a force main reliability program?
correctAnswer: Break history, pressure records, age and material, and inspection findings for each main
explanation: Reliability decisions rest on how each main has performed and what condition it is in. Breaks, pressures, age, material and inspection findings show that performance directly.
options: Break history, pressure records, age and material, and inspection findings for each main
The names of the contractors who installed each main and the dates their invoices were paid
The colour of each valve chamber lid and the mowing schedule for the surface above the main
Fuel receipts for the portable pumps stored at the yard for emergency use at any station
optionA: Break history, pressure records, age and material, and inspection findings for each main
optionB: The names of the contractors who installed each main and the dates their invoices were paid
optionC: The colour of each valve chamber lid and the mowing schedule for the surface above the main

question: Sulfide generation inside a long force main increases most when which combination of conditions occurs?
correctAnswer: Warm sewage, long detention time and low dissolved oxygen inside the force main
explanation: Sulfide forms under anaerobic conditions, so warmth, long detention and low dissolved oxygen together favour generation. Cold sewage, short detention and oxygen all work against it.
options: Warm sewage, long detention time and low dissolved oxygen inside the force main
Cold sewage, short detention time and high dissolved oxygen inside the force main
Warm sewage, short detention time and frequent high velocity scouring of the main
Cold sewage, long detention time and a main that is pressure tested every month
optionA: Warm sewage, long detention time and low dissolved oxygen inside the force main
optionB: Cold sewage, short detention time and high dissolved oxygen inside the force main
optionC: Warm sewage, short detention time and frequent high velocity scouring of the main
optionD: Cold sewage, long detention time and a main that is pressure tested every month
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Hydrogen Sulfide

question: Blockages cluster in a commercial district with many restaurants. Which sources does a FOG program inventory first?
correctAnswer: Food service establishments and other premises that discharge grease bearing wastewater
explanation: Food service establishments are the dominant grease source in a commercial district, so the inventory starts there. Houses, storm basins and construction sites are not the primary FOG sources.
options: Food service establishments and other premises that discharge grease bearing wastewater
Single family homes on the streets at the far edge of the district, inventoried house by house
The storm sewer catch basins along the main street through the middle of the district
Construction sites that are active in the district during the current building season
optionA: Food service establishments and other premises that discharge grease bearing wastewater
optionB: Single family homes on the streets at the far edge of the district, inventoried house by house
optionC: The storm sewer catch basins along the main street through the middle of the district
optionD: Construction sites that are active in the district during the current building season

question: Crews report that manhole locations in the field do not match the office map in several neighbourhoods. Which action fixes the root problem at system scale?
correctAnswer: Field verify the locations and update the asset inventory and mapping records
explanation: A verified inventory and map is the shared record every crew and planner relies on. Personal notes and redraws from memory keep the error in the system, and assets in service cannot simply be marked abandoned.
options: Ask each crew to keep a personal notebook of the locations they happen to remember
Field verify the locations and update the asset inventory and mapping records
Redraw the office map from memory at the end of the construction season each year
Mark the mismatched manholes as abandoned so the map no longer needs to show them

optionB: Field verify the locations and update the asset inventory and mapping records
optionC: Redraw the office map from memory at the end of the construction season each year
optionD: Mark the mismatched manholes as abandoned so the map no longer needs to show them

question: An overflow response plan assigns a specific first duty to the operator who arrives first at an overflow. Which duty is it?
correctAnswer: Contain the overflow where possible and notify the designated supervisor promptly
explanation: First response priorities are containment and notification, so cleanup and reporting can be organized quickly. A full report, waiting idle, or leaving the site all delay those first duties.
options: Complete the full written investigation report before contacting anyone about the event
Contain the overflow where possible and notify the designated supervisor promptly
Wait at the site entrance until a second crew arrives with additional barricades and signs
Leave the site to collect water samples from the treatment plant influent channel first

question: Repairs in one basin removed many private side defects, yet wet weather flows there stayed high. What is the most likely next investigation step?
correctAnswer: Check public side sources such as leaking manholes and cross connections in that basin
explanation: If private side removal does not lower wet weather flow, the remaining I&I is likely entering from public side sources. Repeating finished work, blaming the monitor without checks, or abandoning the basin wastes the study already done.
options: Repeat the same private side repairs a second time and compare the invoices with the first round
Check public side sources such as leaking manholes and cross connections in that basin
Conclude that the basin flow monitor must be faulty and remove it from service for the season
Stop all further investigation in the basin and move the whole program to another sewershed

optionB: Check public side sources such as leaking manholes and cross connections in that basin
optionC: Conclude that the basin flow monitor must be faulty and remove it from service for the season
optionD: Stop all further investigation in the basin and move the whole program to another sewershed

question: One sub-basin shows a sharp flow peak that tracks rainfall closely, while a neighbouring sub-basin shows a slow rise lasting two days after rain. What does the sharp peak most likely indicate?
correctAnswer: Direct inflow sources such as roof leaders or cross connections close to the monitor
explanation: A peak that rises and falls with the rain itself points to direct inflow connections with a fast response. Groundwater infiltration responds slowly over days, and growth or sediment do not track a single storm.
options: Deep groundwater infiltration entering slowly through joints below the water table
Direct inflow sources such as roof leaders or cross connections close to the monitor
A gradual rise in sanitary base flow caused by population growth over several years
Sediment deposits in the trunk sewer slowly releasing stored flow after the storm
optionA: Deep groundwater infiltration entering slowly through joints below the water table
optionB: Direct inflow sources such as roof leaders or cross connections close to the monitor
optionC: A gradual rise in sanitary base flow caused by population growth over several years
optionD: Sediment deposits in the trunk sewer slowly releasing stored flow after the storm

question: Pump starts per hour at one station doubled after a new subdivision connected, while pump condition tests remain normal. What should the operator check first?
correctAnswer: Whether the added inflow has outgrown the wet well working volume and control settings
explanation: More inflow into the same working volume fills the well faster and shortens each cycle, doubling starts. Checking the volume and level settings against the new inflow addresses the cause.
options: Whether the pump motors were painted during the last station refurbishment program
Whether the added inflow has outgrown the wet well working volume and control settings
Whether the station ventilation fan is set to run during the daytime hours only
Whether the spare impeller stored at the station matches the colour of the installed one
optionA: Whether the pump motors were painted during the last station refurbishment program
optionB: Whether the added inflow has outgrown the wet well working volume and control settings
optionC: Whether the station ventilation fan is set to run during the daytime hours only
optionD: Whether the spare impeller stored at the station matches the colour of the installed one

question: Operating pressure on a force main has risen steadily over a year at unchanged flow and unchanged pump condition. Which cause should be investigated first?
correctAnswer: Air accumulation or partial blockage that is reducing the effective diameter of the main
explanation: Rising pressure at the same flow means rising resistance inside the main, which trapped air or partial blockage produces. Sewage density changes, exterior paint and bearing lubricant do not explain a steady pressure trend.
options: A slow decrease in the density of the sewage being pumped from the upstream wet well
Air accumulation or partial blockage that is reducing the effective diameter of the main
Wear on the paint coating applied to the outside of the above ground piping sections
A change in the brand of lubricant used on the pump bearings at the lift station
optionA: A slow decrease in the density of the sewage being pumped from the upstream wet well
optionB: Air accumulation or partial blockage that is reducing the effective diameter of the main
optionC: Wear on the paint coating applied to the outside of the above ground piping sections
optionD: A change in the brand of lubricant used on the pump bearings at the lift station
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual

question: Odour complaints cluster at the manhole where a long force main discharges into a gravity sewer. Which control targets the cause most directly?
correctAnswer: Chemical feed at the upstream station to limit sulfide formation during detention in the main
explanation: Sulfide forms during the long detention in the force main, so treatment at the upstream station prevents formation. Coatings, window advice and yard ventilation do not change conditions inside the main.
options: Painting the inside of the discharge manhole with a scented coating each spring and fall season
Chemical feed at the upstream station to limit sulfide formation during detention in the main
Asking residents near the manhole to keep windows closed during warm weather afternoons
Increasing the ventilation rate in the office building at the upstream lift station yard
optionA: Painting the inside of the discharge manhole with a scented coating each spring and fall season
optionB: Chemical feed at the upstream station to limit sulfide formation during detention in the main
optionC: Asking residents near the manhole to keep windows closed during warm weather afternoons
optionD: Increasing the ventilation rate in the office building at the upstream lift station yard

question: A food service establishment has caused two grease related backups in six months despite having a correctly sized interceptor. What is the most effective program response?
correctAnswer: Shorten its inspection and pump out interval and verify the cleaning records at each visit
explanation: A correctly sized interceptor that is not cleaned on time still passes grease. Shortening the service interval and verifying records addresses the actual failure, which is maintenance frequency.
options: Exempt the premises from further inspections because its interceptor is correctly sized
Shorten its inspection and pump out interval and verify the cleaning records at each visit
Require the premises to install a second interceptor of the same size beside the first one
Move the establishment to the bottom of the inspection list to reward its equipment investment

optionB: Shorten its inspection and pump out interval and verify the cleaning records at each visit
optionC: Require the premises to install a second interceptor of the same size beside the first one

question: A manager must split next year budget between cleaning, CCTV inspection and lining. Which basis best defends the proposed split?
correctAnswer: Condition and risk results showing where each activity reduces the most failures
explanation: Linking each activity to the failures it prevents makes the split defensible and effective. Equal splits, preferences and quotation order ignore where the risk actually sits.
options: An equal three way split of the budget, repeated every year regardless of system results
The personal preferences of the longest serving crew leaders in each of the three work areas
Condition and risk results showing where each activity reduces the most failures
The order in which the three supplier quotations happened to arrive during budget week

question: An annual CMOM review shows overflows per 100 km of sewer rising, while the cleaning program reports 100 percent completion of its schedule. What is the soundest management response?
correctAnswer: Investigate whether cleaning is targeted at the segments that actually cause the overflows
explanation: Completing a schedule is an output, while overflows are the outcome the program exists to prevent. Rising overflows with full completion point to targeting, not effort, as the problem to investigate.
options: Congratulate the cleaning crews and close the review, since the schedule was fully completed
Cancel the cleaning program for a year to see whether the overflow trend changes on its own
Investigate whether cleaning is targeted at the segments that actually cause the overflows
Report the overflow increase as a data error, because a completed schedule cannot allow overflows

question: Basin A removal work costs 4 dollars per litre per day of I&I removed, while Basin B costs 11 dollars for the same unit, and both basins exceed the I&I target. Which sequencing is most defensible?
correctAnswer: Fund Basin A removal first, then reassess Basin B against the updated flow results
explanation: Lower cost per unit of I&I removed buys more flow reduction from the same budget, so Basin A goes first. Higher unit cost does not prove severity, and equal splits or delays ignore the measured economics.
options: Fund Basin B first because its higher unit cost shows that its defects must be more severe
Split the funds evenly between the basins each year until both projects finish together
Fund Basin A removal first, then reassess Basin B against the updated flow results
Delay both basins until a year when the unit costs happen to become equal to each other
optionA: Fund Basin B first because its higher unit cost shows that its defects must be more severe
optionB: Split the funds evenly between the basins each year until both projects finish together
optionC: Fund Basin A removal first, then reassess Basin B against the updated flow results
optionD: Delay both basins until a year when the unit costs happen to become equal to each other

question: A calibrated RDII model matches large storm peaks well but consistently overpredicts the peaks from small storms. What should the analyst adjust first?
correctAnswer: The fast response inflow component, which dominates the sewer response to small events
explanation: Small storms produce a response dominated by fast inflow, so a small storm bias points at that component. The slow component, base flow pattern and a verified gauge do not explain the pattern.
options: The slow groundwater component, which controls flows in the weeks after a storm has passed
The dry weather base flow pattern, which is set by water use inside buildings each day
The fast response inflow component, which dominates the sewer response to small events
The rainfall gauge calibration, which was verified against two nearby gauges last month
optionA: The slow groundwater component, which controls flows in the weeks after a storm has passed
optionB: The dry weather base flow pattern, which is set by water use inside buildings each day
optionC: The fast response inflow component, which dominates the sewer response to small events
optionD: The rainfall gauge calibration, which was verified against two nearby gauges last month

question: A station loses utility power twice each winter. Its generator starts reliably, but fuel runs low partway through the second day of an outage. What is the priority fix?
correctAnswer: Increase on site fuel storage or arrange a guaranteed refuelling arrangement for long outages
explanation: The failure point is fuel endurance, not starting reliability. More storage or a refuelling arrangement extends run time, while a same size replacement, setpoint changes and panel location do not.
options: Replace the generator with a newer unit of the same fuel capacity at the next budget cycle
Reduce the wet well level setpoints so the pumps run less often during the winter months
Increase on site fuel storage or arrange a guaranteed refuelling arrangement for long outages
Move the station alarm panel to a room where staff can hear it more easily during outages
optionA: Replace the generator with a newer unit of the same fuel capacity at the next budget cycle
optionB: Reduce the wet well level setpoints so the pumps run less often during the winter months
optionC: Increase on site fuel storage or arrange a guaranteed refuelling arrangement for long outages
optionD: Move the station alarm panel to a room where staff can hear it more easily during outages

question: Impact damage consistent with water hammer appears at a station after a pump trip event. Which measure addresses the surge most directly?
correctAnswer: Review and service the air and vacuum valves and the surge control devices on the main
explanation: Air and vacuum valves and surge devices exist to control the pressure transients that cause water hammer damage. Faster starts can worsen transients, and painting or level changes do not control surge.
options: Increase the speed of the pump start sequence so the main refills as quickly as possible
Paint the damaged fittings and return the main to service without any further checking
Review and service the air and vacuum valves and the surge control devices on the main
Lower the wet well stop level so the pumps draw the well down further on every cycle
optionA: Increase the speed of the pump start sequence so the main refills as quickly as possible
optionB: Paint the damaged fittings and return the main to service without any further checking
optionC: Review and service the air and vacuum valves and the surge control devices on the main
optionD: Lower the wet well stop level so the pumps draw the well down further on every cycle

question: Concrete above the waterline in a wet well is softening and losing material, while the submerged concrete remains sound. What is driving the damage?
correctAnswer: Hydrogen sulfide released into the headspace is converting to acid on the moist concrete surface
explanation: Damage concentrated above the waterline is the classic pattern of sulfide corrosion, where gas released to the headspace forms acid on moist surfaces. Even attack, sunlight and splashing do not match that pattern.
options: Chloride in the sewage is dissolving the concrete evenly across the whole depth of the wet well
Ultraviolet light entering through the hatch is breaking down the surface of the concrete
Hydrogen sulfide released into the headspace is converting to acid on the moist concrete surface
The concrete is being worn away by the splashing of the influent as it enters the wet well
optionA: Chloride in the sewage is dissolving the concrete evenly across the whole depth of the wet well
optionB: Ultraviolet light entering through the hatch is breaking down the surface of the concrete
optionC: Hydrogen sulfide released into the headspace is converting to acid on the moist concrete surface
optionD: The concrete is being worn away by the splashing of the influent as it enters the wet well
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Hydrogen Sulfide

question: Grease blockages repeat on one residential street, and there are no food businesses anywhere nearby. Which program step fits the source best?

explanation: With no commercial source, household disposal practices are the likely contributor, supported by segment inspection to confirm buildup. Citywide commercial mail outs and end of pipe interceptors do not fit a residential source.

Installation of a large interceptor at the downstream end of the street sewer at city expense
Targeted household education combined with inspection of the problem segment for grease buildup
Adding the street to the list of segments that receive no cleaning until a blockage is reported

optionD: Adding the street to the list of segments that receive no cleaning until a blockage is reported

question: A trunk sewer reaches 85 percent of its capacity at peak wet weather flow, and a large development is proposed in its basin. What decision protects the system?
correctAnswer: Require capacity improvements or a phased connection before the added flow is accepted
explanation: At 85 percent of capacity in wet weather, added flow can push the trunk into surcharge. Capacity work or phasing protects the system, while timing and service size do not change the added volume.

Ask the developer to connect during the winter, when construction crews are less busy
Approve the connection if the developer agrees to use smaller diameter service pipes

question: After a major storm, several overflows occur at different sites across the city. Beyond the response itself, what does strong CMOM leadership ensure happens for each event?
correctAnswer: Each event is documented and reported through the channels that provincial requirements set out
explanation: Provincial requirements expect overflow events to be documented and reported individually. Verbal summaries, combined lines and complaint driven reporting leave the record incomplete.

Each event is combined into a single report line, regardless of the sites or causes involved
Each event is reported only if a member of the public phones in a complaint about that site

question: A program can fund six flow monitors for a 40 km basin study. Where do the monitors produce the most useful I&I data?
correctAnswer: At sub-basin outlets chosen so that each monitored area can be compared with the others
explanation: Comparable sub-basin data is what lets a study rank areas and target removal. Clustered, age based or convenience based placement cannot separate one area from another.
options: All six side by side at the basin outlet, so the readings can be averaged for accuracy
At the six oldest manholes in the basin, regardless of the areas that drain through them
At whichever manholes are closest to the road, so the crews can reach them most quickly

The flow monitor battery is weakening each spring and inflating the recorded values

question: Two force mains compete for renewal funds. Main A is older but runs at low pressure beneath a park. Main B is younger, runs at high pressure and crosses a creek. Which ranking logic is soundest?
correctAnswer: Weigh likelihood and consequence together, so Main B may rank first despite its younger age
explanation: Risk combines how likely a failure is with what the failure would cost, and a high pressure creek crossing carries severe consequences. Age, length or cosmetics alone cannot rank renewal need.
options: Weigh likelihood and consequence together, so Main B may rank first despite its younger age
Rank Main A first on age alone, because age is the only factor a renewal program may consider
Rank the mains by the length of pipe involved, starting with whichever main is the longest
Defer both mains and spend the renewal funds on station cosmetics until one of them fails

question: Nitrate feed at a lift station controls odour at the force main outlet, yet corrosion continues in the gravity sewer downstream of the outlet. What is the most likely explanation?
correctAnswer: The chemical is consumed inside the force main, leaving the downstream sewer unprotected

The nitrate has increased the strength of the sewage so much that it now corrodes concrete
The gravity sewer is corroding because its slope is too flat for the flows it now carries
The corrosion readings downstream are being taken by a different crew than the upstream ones

Expand the same program citywide a second time and assume the district will catch up later
Remove the district from the program statistics so the citywide result looks more consistent
Replace every interceptor in the district at city expense without checking any records first

Small flows move so slowly through a drop that sediment permanently blocks the outlet pipe
